findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && so admins are rejected
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. `isTeamAdmin` already covers ADMIN and OWNER roles, so the `&&` effectively requires the user to be an owner. Team admins who are neither organizer nor attendee get FORBIDDEN, contradicting the variable name. This should be `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: The EventManager is built from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The caller can be an attendee or a team admin/owner rather than the organizer. In that case `updateCalendarAttendees` runs against the wrong user's calendar credentials, so the organizer's external calendar event and its references are not updated or the call fails. The organizer's credentials (`booking.user`) should be used.

findings.title: Calendar update failure after DB write leaves inconsistent state
findings.body: The attendees are committed to the database first via `prisma.booking.update`. Only afterwards is `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` awaited, without a try/catch. If the calendar update throws, the client gets an error and no emails are sent, but the guests are already persisted. A retry then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' because the guests already exist.

findings.title: Emails are sent based on raw input instead of the newly added guests
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the full input list rather than `uniqueGuests`. Input emails that were already attendees (filtered out of the insert) are treated as new guests. They get a fresh 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notification.

findings.title: Case-sensitive comparisons let the blacklist and duplicate checks be bypassed
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased but the guest emails are not, so `Foo@blocked.com` passes `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. The existing-attendee check is also case-sensitive, so a differently cased address is inserted as a duplicate attendee. The server schema does not dedupe input either, so `createMany` can insert duplicates within one request.

findings.title: Unbounded guest list lets any attendee trigger mass emails
findings.body: Any attendee of a booking can call this mutation, and `guests` has no max length or dedupe. The handler also does not check booking status (cancelled or past bookings are accepted). The result is arbitrarily many cal.com emails, carrying calendar invites, to arbitrary addresses. That is a spam/abuse vector. Limit the array size, dedupe on the server, and reject cancelled or past bookings.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disableStandardEmails event-type settings
findings.body: Every other booking email sender respects `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` / `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` from the event-type metadata. The new function takes no metadata and always sends host, team-member and attendee emails. Event types that disabled standard emails will still send them.

findings.title: Error toast fallback never used and the invalid-email flag is never cleared
findings.body: `message` is a template string such as `undefined: ...`, so it is always truthy and the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is dead code. Users may see 'undefined: <raw message>'. Separately, `isInvalidEmail` is only reset by the Cancel button. After fixing the input and submitting successfully, or closing the dialog via overlay/Escape, the error banner persists the next time the dialog opens.

findings.title: Bookings without userId cause an unhandled 500
findings.body: `findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws a Prisma NotFound error when the booking has no user. The client receives an internal server error instead of a meaningful TRPCError.
